summary: Source audit of the 6-cycle common interface; no compute, no Lean. (1) PROVED why m6's naive whole-circle completion violates States.two_state_impossible (States.lean:243): with Angles = AddCircle(2*pi) the six premises match one-for-one - measurability and WeakColoring of a genuine trace field, centre x, J={0,2} and K={3,5} giving |univ\(JuK)| = 2 so hcard holds EXACTLY TIGHT, a measurable side bit s, the two RealState conclusions, and the 60-degree flip - which holds only AT THE SIX SAMPLED ANGLES; the naive completion asserts it a.e., which is what the lemma forbids. So m6 is a finite orbit model, not the restriction of any whole-circle trace field. (2) REDUCTION: no singleton palette is licensed at m=6 since every label lies in some E_i, so any two-palette 6-cycle uses two disjoint 2-sets, whose union leaves exactly 2 labels outside, and two_state_impossible kills it. Every genuine 6-cycle must use AT LEAST THREE palettes. (3) Minimal surviving obstacle proposed: the 3-palette sequence {0,2},{3,5},{1,4},{3,5},{0,2},{3,5}; combinatorial premises checked by hand, sign bits UNVERIFIED and handed to the graph worker. (4) Missing realisation named: a multi-state analogue (MS) for r >= 3, absent from the tree. m5 escapes by the COUNT instead (label 5 outside every interface).

verified_results.statement: PROOF that m6's naive whole-circle completion violates it: k=6 measurable weak colouring and centre x from a genuine trace field; J={0,2}, K={3,5} so univ\\(JuK) = {1,4} and hcard holds with equality; s the side bit; on the J-side the palette is {0,2} a.e. so both RealState inclusions hold, likewise {3,5}; and the palettes alternate at the six angles t+j*pi/3 so the flip holds at those six angles. Completing the flip to a.e. gives all six premises and False.
verified_results.grade: PROOF (mine); the only non-immediate step is identifying the side bit with the RealState level sets

verified_results.statement: hcard is exactly tight for m6: |J u K| = 4 and |univ \\(J u K)| = 2 = the bound. So m6 is the maximal configuration the two-state lemma can still exclude, and two_state_impossible is a boundary marker rather than a refutation of the finite witness.

m6 is a finite orbit model, not the restriction of a whole-circle trace field: the inconsistency is located in the 60-degree flip, which is known only at six angles and not a.e. The finite witness remains valid at its own scope.
LEMMA: at m=6 no singleton palette is licensed, since every label a lies in E_a = {a, a+1 mod 6} and P_j is required not to be contained in any E_i.

THEOREM: every genuine 6-cycle whose palettes take exactly two distinct values is impossible. Proof: singletons are excluded, so both palettes have size 2; adjacency makes them disjoint; union 4 leaves 2 outside so hcard holds; the flip and RealState conditions hold as in the m6 analysis; two_state_impossible gives False. Hence every genuine 6-cycle must use at least three distinct palettes, and F6 at m=6 reduces to excluding 3-or-more-palette 6-cycles.
verified_results.grade: PROOF (mine), resting on the licensed premises as relayed

verified_results.statement: Proposed minimal surviving multi-state obstacle: the 3-palette cyclic sequence {0,2}, {3,5}, {1,4}, {3,5}, {0,2}, {3,5}. Combinatorially checked by hand: all palettes are non-consecutive 2-sets hence not contained in any E_i, and all six adjacent pairs are disjoint. It escapes two_state_impossible through the NUMBER OF STATES, not the count, since |univ\\(AuB)| = |univ\\(BuC)| = 2 would satisfy hcard.
verified_results.grade: proposed; sign-bit conditions UNVERIFIED (handed to the graph worker)

verified_results.statement: The missing analytic realisation is a multi-state analogue (MS) of two_state_impossible for r >= 3. Grep over lean/OAI confirms the tree contains only the two-state lemma (hits at Interfaces.lean:139 and States.lean:378 are applications of it); no three_state or multi_state declaration exists.
verified_results.grade: source-verified absence; the truth of (MS) is open and not claimed

verified_results.statement: Contrast with m=5: there E_i = {i, i+1 mod 5} so the union covers only {0..4} and label 5 lies in no interface, licensing the singleton palette {5}; |J u K| = 3 and |univ \\(J u K)| = 3 > 2, so m5 escapes two_state_impossible through the COUNT. The m=5 and m=6 escapes are therefore of different kinds.

Source-chain correction recorded as given: the sufficient route is L6 AND F6 -> FullApprox6 -> generic cover/mesh contradiction; T6 -> B2 supplies neither; B2 is not a direct hypothesis of HoleApprox once L6 is known. I did not re-derive it and make no claim about L6.
No numerical bound is claimed; no cycle length other than 6 is analysed; no claim that F6 holds or fails; no claim that ternary exclusion or any palette argument gives chi >= 7.

conjectures: F6 at m=6 now rests entirely on excluding 3-plus-palette 6-cycles. If the graph worker's sign-bit test finds a licensed q for the section-4 palette sequence, then no purely combinatorial argument can give F6 at m=6 and a multi-state analytic lemma (MS) becomes necessary; if no q exists, the 3-palette family may be combinatorially empty and F6 at m=6 could be settled by finite enumeration alone.

The contrast m5 (count escape) versus m6 (state escape) suggests the general m-cycle picture is: escape by count whenever some label lies outside every interface, and escape by states only when the interfaces cover the labels. For k=6 that boundary sits exactly at m=6.
